clue.text: Sort of programme producing a comedy turn?

indicators.note: producing tells us the letters of the next words are worked into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A light question about which kind of broadcast might come out of a stand-up comic's act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder: the whole of 'a comedy turn' is rearranged, signalled by 'producing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A factual film or broadcast about real events is a kind of programme.

clue.text: Fixes penalties underpinning limits of divergence

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece underpinning another sits below it, so it comes second
the limits of a word are its two outside letters, first and last

parts.note: fines are monetary penalties

explanation.surface: Someone sets financial sanctions to support the bounds placed on deviation, like a regulator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underpinning' puts FINES below DE, the outside letters of 'divergence'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix the meaning or boundaries of something is to pin it down precisely.

clue.text: Condition experienced by just over half of casino workers?

indicators.note: of a nine-letter word, just over half is its first five letters, so the last four go

parts.note: croupiers run the gaming tables in a casino

explanation.surface: A question about some ailment most staff at a gambling house seem to share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just over half of' keeps five of the nine letters of the croupiers' title.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a childhood illness of the airways with a barking cough, so a medical condition.

clue.text: Doubt Mike is generous

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a giving person is generous

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure whether a friend called Mike is really openhearted.
explanation.definitionFit: A misgiving is a feeling of uncertainty or apprehension, a synonym for doubt.

clue.text: Patriarch showing evident lack of surprise?

parts.note: no as in 'no sign of' marks a plain absence
ah is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A question about a forefather who greets everything with complete calm.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'no ah': no exclamation, so no surprise shown.
explanation.definitionFit: The ark builder of Genesis is one of the biblical patriarchs, father of Shem, Ham and Japheth.

clue.text: Made tough new deal under queen

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece under another comes after it

parts.note: Anne was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of deal are made into a fresh form

explanation.surface: A monarch drove a hard bargain, striking a fresh agreement that left things tougher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges DEAL to ALED, placed under ANNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Annealing metal or glass by heating and slow cooling toughens it and removes brittleness.

clue.text: State needing sycophants with no end of eagerness

indicators.note: with no tells us a letter is dropped from the flatterers

parts.note: yes-men are sycophants who agree with whatever the boss says

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A nation where flatterers abound but none show any keenness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no end of eagerness' removes S, the last letter of 'eagerness', from YESMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: This Arabian country on the Red Sea is a sovereign state.

clue.text: Made a fuss and responded, promoting head of chambers

indicators.note: promoting moves a letter higher up, which in a down answer means to the top

parts.note: to react is to respond

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A barrister kicked up a fuss and answered back when the senior member of chambers was promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting' lifts C, the first letter of 'chambers', from inside REACTED to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal speech, to create is to complain noisily or make a scene.

clue.text: Lie about Republican producing conflict

indicators.note: about means the falsehood goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: fiction is invented untruth, so a lie

explanation.surface: A falsehood about a Republican politician causes political strife.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction is discord or clashing between people, a synonym for conflict.

clue.text: Look serious about good spring that produces life in pond

indicators.note: about means the stern look surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: to frown is to look serious or displeased
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Someone scowls over a fine spring that brings forth creatures in a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' is not the season but a water source, SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: The masses of jelly-coated eggs laid by frogs are the beginnings of pond creatures.

clue.text: Book detective showing bite for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means all but the last letter is taken

parts.note: a morsel is a small bite of food

explanation.surface: A fictional sleuth shows his teeth, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: Colin Dexter's Oxford inspector appears in a series of novels, so a detective from books.

clue.text: Drop off family item used at table

parts.note: to drop off is to fall asleep, to nap
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A relative nods off over dinner, perhaps clutching a family heirloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A serviette is a cloth or paper square used while dining.

clue.text: Son in failing action on women's panel

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another follows it

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the jumble
failing suggests the word action has gone wrong and is jumbled

explanation.surface: A legal action about a son fails before a panel of women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges ACTION; 'in' puts S into it to make AINSCOT, placed after W.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden panelling on the lower part of a room's walls; one section is a panel.

clue.text: Photograph held back by police if lesions?

indicators.note: back says the concealed letters are read backwards
held says the letters are kept within a run of the clue's words
by names the words holding them, the run that follows in the clue

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Police withhold a picture in case it shows injuries.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hiding no indicator: 'held by' conceals the letters and 'back' turns them round, so EIFLES read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-portrait taken with a phone camera is a type of snapshot.

clue.text: Relaxed youth should keep one stern

indicators.note: should keep means the young man holds a letter inside him

parts.note: a lad is a youth
the Roman numeral I is one
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Advice that a young man ought to keep one serious demeanour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' looks like an adjective for strict, but it is the rear of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid-back describes someone easygoing and unhurried, a synonym for relaxed.

clue.text: Spotted dress, oddly, and wept

indicators.note: oddly means the first, third and fifth letters are taken

parts.note: to weep is to cry

explanation.surface: Someone noticed a strange outfit and burst into tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like it describes the dress, but it picks its odd letters, DES.
explanation.definitionFit: To descry is an old literary verb for catching sight of something far off.

clue.text: County's team must see requirement for bottle?

parts.note: Cork is an Irish county, here with its possessive
a crew is a team, as of rowers

explanation.surface: A county sports side has to find what it needs for a bottle, perhaps of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' here is a wine bottle, which needs an opener.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral opener is needed to draw the stopper from a bottle of wine.

clue.text: State of turmoil may see king wearing fancy panties

indicators.note: wearing means the monarch is dressed in the garment, so placed inside it
fancy means elaborate, signalling a rearrangement of panties

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Chaos might ensue if a monarch were seen in frilly underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges PANTIES, and 'wearing' puts K inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit of serpents is a figurative scene of chaos and vicious struggle.

clue.text: Calling on Conservative behaving very humbly

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another comes after it

parts.note: ringing someone is calling them on the phone

explanation.surface: Phoning a Tory and being terribly deferential.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowering obsequiously or fawning is behaving with exaggerated humility.

clue.text: Leaves a couple of books impounded?

indicators.note: the question mark signals that the pen word also holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to impound is to shut in a pound or cage
B is the abbreviation for book, so two books are BB

explanation.surface: Someone departs as a pair of library volumes are seized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impounded' does double duty, a semi-cryptic touch the question mark flags: it names the pen and shuts A and two books inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A head of this vegetable is a tight ball of edible greens, hence leaves.

clue.text: Ditch or river full of fish? Quite the contrary

indicators.note: full of signals one piece is placed inside another
quite the contrary swaps the roles, so the creature contains the waterway

parts.note: a tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A question about a ditch or stream teeming with fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the contrary' reverses 'river full of fish' so the fish TENCH holds R.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, narrow excavation in the ground is a kind of ditch.

clue.text: Match needs this from striker — an impetuous type!

definitions.meaning: a match struck on the box gets a burning tip

explanation.surface: A footballer must be fiery to win the game, but turns out reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' looks like a footballer, but it is whoever strikes a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The burning tip of a match, and an informal word for someone who acts rashly.

clue.text: Elderly Russian's bleat about President Kennedy initially

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is', so this means an old Russian woman is

indicators.note: about means the bleat goes round the other pieces

parts.note: baa is a sheep's bleat
Bush was a US president, father or son

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

explanation.surface: An old Russian bleats on about American presidents.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Russian's' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In Russian the word means grandmother, and in English it describes an old Russian woman.

clue.text: Attack head of secondary school

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word secondary

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A secondary school headteacher comes under assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of secondary school' looks like a headteacher, but 'head of' gives just S.
explanation.definitionFit: To set upon someone is to assault them, a phrasal verb meaning attack.

clue.text: Agree to see hospital dept on a case of sinusitis

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another comes after it
the case of a word is its outside letters, first and last

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A patient agrees to visit the ear, nose and throat clinic for sinusitis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the department after the other pieces in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To give consent or approval is to agree.

clue.text: Duck (down under it as cover)

parts.note: the bird's name, followed by the word down, gives a bed cover filled with its feathers

explanation.surface: A sea bird whose soft feathers are used beneath it as a covering.
explanation.walkthrough: Put 'down' after the bird's name and you get a quilt, the cover of the bracket.
explanation.definitionFit: This large sea duck gives its soft breast feathers to stuff quilts.

clue.text: Couple caught out Bank of Scotland

indicators.note: out means the letter goes missing

parts.note: a brace is a couple, as of game birds
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A pair is dismissed while dealing with a famous Scottish bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank of Scotland' looks like the lender, but it is a hillside in Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish dialect the word is a steep slope or hillside by a river.

clue.text: A way to incorporate business course

indicators.note: to incorporate means the road takes another piece inside it

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A method for building a company into a business studies course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a racecourse, not a programme of study.
explanation.definitionFit: This Berkshire venue for the Royal meeting is a famous racecourse.

clue.text: Flyer parking free in great convertible

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
convertible means the word great can be changed into another form

parts.note: to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A pilot finds free parking for a splendid open-topped car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' looks like a car, but it is the anagram signal; 'in' places the freeing word inside the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A game bird is a flying creature, and flyer is a playful word for any bird.

clue.text: Hell — could be clear the girl's promise crosses line

parts.note: net as in clear profit after deductions
her means belonging to that girl

indicators.note: crosses means the pledge spans a letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a word is a promise, as in 'giving one's word'

explanation.surface: Torment might follow if a girl breaks her vow by overstepping a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The underworld of the dead is a name for the infernal regions.
